You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I work at one of the drone operating companies. My job as a fleet technician is to keep our drones and charging equipment in working order, which involves adding new drones, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back, and sending drones to charge. Regulators can also ask us to show how our drones have been looked after.
The question: Could you walk me through a typical shift—what do you do first thing when you start, what keeps you busy during the day, and how do you wrap up?

The question: Let's look at the tasks you mentioned—like taking drones out of service, putting them back, or sending them to charge. How do you find out which drones need your attention?

Q12
The answer just before it: I set up our charging pads at our sites, and I also send drones to charge. We have our own charging pads at our sites, a few dozen of them, which use specific charging connectors that are not interchangeable.
The question: What happens if someone tries to send a drone to a charging pad that doesn't have the right connector, or how do you prevent that?

Q13
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Besides the connector type, what else differs between your drones or your charging pads?

Q14
The answer just before it: Our drones are of several models from different manufacturers, differing in how much they can carry, how far they can fly on a full battery, which sensors they carry, and which charging connector they use. We also have charging equipment and charging pads at our sites, with several connector types in use that are not interchangeable.
The question: How many drones are in your fleet, and how do you keep track of where each one is and whether it is working or in repair?

Q15
The answer just before it: We run a few hundred drones and a few dozen charging pads at our sites. I take drones out of service for repairs and put them back, and I also add new drones and retire old ones. I don't know how to keep track of where each one is.
The question: Is there anything else you can tell me about your sites, your repairs, or how your company works with the platform?

Q16
The answer just before it: Each company runs its own systems, such as billing and customer updates, that need to hear about what happens to its drones and jobs. Our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and regulators can ask a company to show how its drones have been looked after. Each of our sites has a few dozen charging pads, and each drone has a home site.
The question: Can a drone charge or be serviced at a site that is not its home site?

Q17
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Can you tell me more about what your company's own systems need to hear about when things happen to your drones?

Q18
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Is there anything else about your role, the drones, the sites, or the charging equipment that we haven't covered yet?
